selected_mechanism.name: CMS Rural Health Transformation Program — Alaska DOH Subrecipient Award Gate

news_trigger.verbatim_quote: Mid-July: Notification of final funding decisions for implementation pathway applicants. Final funding decisions are made by the DOH Commissioner.
news_trigger.outlet: State of Alaska Department of Health (RHTP program page)

selected_mechanism.one_line_definition: A $272.2M Year-1 federal capital flow (CMS Rural Health Transformation Program) that enters Alaska through a single state recipient (DOH), whose Commissioner makes the binary award/deny decision on 403 implementation applicants, deciding which tribal health corporations and health-IT/AI vendors are funded to build the state's FHIR-native rural health data infrastructure.

layers.what_it_does: Obligates Year-1 RHTP capital to a single per-state recipient; sets the budget period and CMS compliance rails on how it may be spent.
layers.controlling_actor: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), Office of Acquisition and Grants (institutional role)
layers.reverify_note: TAGGS confirms award number RHTCMS332062, recipient State of Alaska Department of Health, $272,174,856 FY2026, awarding agency CMS, Assistance Listing 93798 Rural Health Transformation Program.

layers.what_it_does: Lead agency that sets priorities, runs the application process, and makes the final binary award/deny decision on each subrecipient application; the Advisory Council only shapes recommendations.
layers.controlling_actor: Alaska Department of Health — DOH Commissioner (institutional role; recipient of award RHTCMS332062)
layers.reverify_note: DOH page states verbatim 'Final funding decisions are made by the DOH Commissioner' and lays out the 'June 22 - mid-July: DOH review' followed by 'Mid-July: Notification of final funding decisions' timeline.

layers.what_it_does: Runs the LOI intake, application portal, and subaward issuance/management on DOH's behalf, but is explicitly stripped of decision authority.
layers.controlling_actor: The Alaska Community Foundation (contracted administrator; institutional role)
layers.reverify_note: State public notice confirms 'The Department of Health is partnering with the Alaska Community Foundation to administer subrecipient application and award processes'; DOH page adds ACF 'does not make final funding decisions.'

layers.what_it_does: Execute the funded builds; the shared tribal EHR/interoperability backbone is the substrate any FHIR-native rural-health data/AI build must integrate against.
layers.controlling_actor: Tribal health corporations and health-IT/AI vendors among the 403 implementation applicants (ANTHC, Southcentral Foundation, YKHC, SEARHC and vendor subrecipients)
layers.reverify_note: DOH page confirms the subrecipient pool: '403 organizations advanced to submit full applications' (implementation) and '28 organizations preliminarily approved' (planning). NOTE: the specific 'ANTHC Oracle Health domain carries ~two-thirds of tribal outpatient encounters' figure is NOT established on this page; it is contextual, not the sourced structural fact of this layer.

chokepoint.binary_decision: Award or deny each of the 403 implementation-pathway applications, allocating the ~$272M Year-1 pool in the mid-July 2026 notification.
chokepoint.why_asymmetric: This is a single-officer decision, not a committee: the primary source explicitly places final authority with the DOH Commissioner, strips the Alaska Community Foundation of any decision role ('does not make final funding decisions'), and reduces CMS to compliance rails and the Advisory Council to recommendations. One state officer decides who anchors Alaska's rural-health data infrastructure.

selected_mechanism.structural_read: This mechanism is a federal-to-state capital funnel that narrows, by design, to one state officer. CMS obligates a fixed $272M Year-1 tranche and then steps back to compliance oversight; the Alaska Community Foundation runs the plumbing but is contractually barred from deciding; the Advisory Council advises. The single point where the money actually turns into a build is the DOH Commissioner's award decision. For Alaska that means the interoperability spine of rural health, and whatever AI/analytics layer eventually sits on top of it, is being routed this week through a single state grant decision, not through a market or a competitive federal process. Whoever wins these subawards inherits a multi-year, standards-setting position in the state's health-data architecture.
selected_mechanism.forward_implication: The mid-July 2026 award notifications land this week and the Year-1 budget period closes 10/30/2026. Health-IT/AI vendors and tribal health corporations positioned as (or partnered with) named subrecipients should confirm award status now and lock integration commitments to the dominant tribal EHR backbone before the budget period compresses; allocators tracking Alaska health-data infrastructure should treat the DOH award list, once published, as the definitive map of who holds the FHIR-native buildout.

_validation_note: Selected C1 (RHTP) as the single load-bearing pick. Reverified all four layers by fetching primary sources: TAGGS confirmed CMS award RHTCMS332062 / $272,174,856 to Alaska DOH; the DOH program page confirmed verbatim 'Final funding decisions are made by the DOH Commissioner' plus the mid-July final-funding-decision timeline and the 403-implementation / 28-planning applicant pool; the state public notice and DOH page confirmed the Alaska Community Foundation as administrator explicitly barred from decision authority. News tie is the strongest available at 14 days because the mid-July final funding decision is a live, this-week event (today 2026-07-10). Chokepoint asymmetry is clean: one state officer (DOH Commissioner) owns the binary award/deny. Mechanism-not-actor holds. Honesty caveat: the DOH page confirms the 403-applicant subrecipient layer but does NOT source the 'ANTHC Oracle domain carries two-thirds of encounters' figure, treated as context, not a sourced fact. Window was NOT broadened; a valid 14-day target cleared all seven points.
